title: OTF (Open Tab Format)
description: OTF is the Bluegrass Songbook's tab format: one JSON document per tab, usually stored as *.otf.json. VERSION RULE. otf_version is "MAJOR.MINOR"; "1.0" is the shape as of G15a (2026-10-28); "1.1" adds the optional metadata.tab_by; "1.2" adds dynamics (tracks[].dyn, note.dyn), the "bend" effect, measure_marks, chords and chord_diagrams; "1.3" adds annotations[].track, annotations[].kind and annotations[].place. Adding an OPTIONAL field bumps the minor version. Anything else (a rename, a removal, a change of meaning, a new required field) bumps the major version. Files of any earlier 1.x stay valid under the current schema. Writers stamp the current version; readers accept any 1.x and reject any other major. The order of properties in this file is the canonical key order used when a document is written out (G15b). Keys starting with an underscore are runtime view caches and are never valid in a file. Some rules JSON Schema cannot express are enforced by both validators (scripts/lib/otf_schema.py and validateOTF in docs/js/otf-editor/otf-validate.js); they are listed in docs/schema/otf.md.

otf_version.description: Format version, "MAJOR.MINOR". Any "1.x" is accepted; see the version rule in this schema's description.

metadata.description: What the tab is: title, time signature, tempo, and optional credits.

time_signature.description: Default time signature for every measure, as "beats/unit" ("4/4", "6/8"). Measures listed in time_signature_changes override it for that measure only.

tempo.description: Tempo in quarter-note beats per minute.

key.description: Key of the tune, as written by the source ("G", "Am"). May be empty.

composer.description: Composer or arranger credit. May be empty.

tab_by.description: Who wrote this tab (added in 1.1): a name and an optional link, e.g. their Banjo Hangout profile. Not the song's composer.

name.description: The tab writer's name: non-empty, no leading or trailing whitespace, at most 100 characters.

url.description: Optional link, http or https only, at most 500 characters.

time_signature_changes.description: Per-measure time signature overrides. Each entry applies ONLY to its own measure; every other measure follows metadata.time_signature.

measure.description: 1-based measure number the override applies to.

timing.description: The tick grid every tick and duration in the document is measured on.

ticks_per_beat.description: Ticks in one beat, where a beat is a quarter note (480 in every file so far). A measure of n/d is n*4/d beats long.

tracks.description: The instruments in the tab. Each may have a matching key in notation.

id.description: Track id, unique in the document. It is the key of this track's notation.

instrument.description: Instrument name as the source gave it ("5-string-banjo", "mandolin", "percussion", ...). Free text.

tuning.description: Open-string pitches, string 1 first ("D4"). Its length is the track's string count. Empty only on a percussion track, which counts lines instead.

role.description: What the track does in the arrangement.

dyn.description: The track's usual dynamic level (added in 1.2), loudest first: fff ff f mf mp p pp (TablEdit codes 0-6). A track with no dyn is at f. A note's own dyn appears only when it differs from its track's.

percussion.description: True on a percussion track. Requires lines.

lines.description: Number of staff lines (instruments) on a percussion track; its notes' s counts against this instead of the tuning length.

notation.description: The music: {trackId: [measure, ...]}. Every key must name a track; a track may have no key (an empty track).

measure.description: 1-based measure number. Unique and ascending within a track.

events.description: Moments in the measure that have notes, ascending by tick.

tick.description: Offset from the start of the measure, in ticks. Unique and ascending within a measure, and inside the measure's length.

notes.description: Notes struck at this tick, at most one per string.

annotations.description: Placed text (chord names, section labels, remarks), each on a track's staff, above it unless place says below.

tick.description: Offset inside that measure, in ticks.

track.description: Id of the track the text belongs to (added in 1.3; rule annotation_track). A text draws on its own track only. Absent means a text from before 1.3, or from a file that says nothing about tracks; the renderer draws it on the first pitched track.

kind.description: What the text is (added in 1.3): "text" or "chord" (text is a chord name as written). Absent means "text".

place.description: Where the text sits against its staff (added in 1.3): "above" or "below". Absent means "above".

reading_list.description: Playback order: measure ranges to play, in order (repeats and jumps unrolled). Absent means play straight through.

from_measure.description: First measure of the range, inclusive.

to_measure.description: Last measure of the range, inclusive. A range running past the last written measure is a warning, not an error (#263).

measure_marks.description: Repeat signs and other TablEdit measure flags (added in 1.2): one entry per marked measure, strictly ascending by measure (TablEdit ORs several marks into one). They are drawn and kept; playback follows reading_list only. The decoded fields must agree with raw (rule mark_raw).

repeat_start.description: A repeat starts at the beginning of this measure. raw & 0x40.

repeat_end.description: A repeat ends at the end of this measure. raw & 0x80.

ending.description: Numbered ending bracket ("1." ... "6.") over this measure: raw & 7 when it is 1-6. Absent for 0 and for 7 ("unspecified", drawn as nothing).

jump.description: Jump mark: da-signo (raw & 0x38 = 0x10), signo (0x18), al-coda (0x20) or coda (0x28).

end_bar.description: A thin-thick end bar at the end of the measure, a repeat end without the dots. (raw & 0x38) == 0x08.

raw.description: TablEdit's flag byte for this measure, 0-255, kept so anything not modelled (ending 7, a repeat count) round-trips exactly.

chords.description: The chord-diagram table (added in 1.2), as in TablEdit: chord_diagrams[].chord is an index into this list. Records no diagram uses are kept so the table round-trips. A name-only record has no frets.

frets.description: One item per string, string 1 first: the absolute fret, 0 = open, null = not played.

items.description: Fret 0-31, or null for a string that is not played.

fingers.description: Left-hand finger 1-4 per string (null = none), the same length as frets. Needs frets (rule chord_fingers).

first_fret.description: First fret shown, a signed byte (TablEdit draws "fr." when it is above 1).

chord_diagrams.description: Where chord diagrams are drawn (added in 1.2): above a track's staff at a measure and tick, each pointing at a record in chords.

tick.description: Offset inside that measure, in ticks; must lie inside the measure (rule chord_tick).

track.description: Id of the track whose staff carries the diagram (rule chord_track).

dx.description: Horizontal nudge from the anchor, a signed byte.

dy.description: Vertical nudge from the anchor, a signed byte.

x_source.description: Provenance of the tab (type, source_id, author, url, converted_at, ...). Free-form: the only object in the format that accepts unknown keys. `skipped` (G15e) is {key: count}, written by the .tef importers only when at least one count is non-zero, and shown to the reader as "Not kept from this file: ..." (docs/js/tef-skipped.js). Keys, in this order, with the label readers see: tempo_changes = tempo changes; instrument_changes = instrument (MIDI) changes; scale_diagrams = scale diagrams; accents = accent and crescendo marks; slurs = slurs and brackets; picking_marks = picking marks not on a note; special_characters = special characters and musical signs; percussion = percussion marks; chord_diagrams = chord diagrams (only when a V2 chord table fails to parse); free_text = lines of free text (V3 header pointer 0x4C: a free-text block of the file's notes, which some tabbers fill with song words or chords; its TablEdit UI name is not confirmed, and no real lyrics component has been found; V2 files are not counted); tapping = tapping amounts; vibrato = vibrato amounts; tremolo_bar = tremolo-bar amounts (the mark is kept as fx, the amount is not); other = other TablEdit markings (a component type the importer does not recognise). Deliberately not counted: voices, rests, stem and beam layout, and line breaks and spacing/layout marks, because none of them changes what the tab says; per-track volume and pan, because the track bytes that hold them are unknown. The submit step drops x_source, so skipped never reaches works/.

note.description: One note: a string and a fret, plus optional articulation. Property order here is the canonical key order for a note.

s.description: String number, 1 = the first tuning entry. Must not exceed the track's string count (or lines, for percussion).

tie.description: True when this note is tied to the previous note on the same string.

tech.description: Left-hand technique into this note: h hammer-on, p pull-off, / slide up, \ slide down, x dead (muted) note, b bend.

fx.description: Per-note effects, a set stored in this canonical order. Omitted when empty. "bend" (added in 1.2) bends the note up and holds; "bend-release" bends up and comes back down. Neither has an amount field: the amount is the next note on the same string, which is the bend target (tech "b").

grace.description: A grace note leading into this note. It has no tick of its own.

f.description: Fret of the grace note, 0 = open.

kind.description: How the grace note connects to the main note. Absent means a plain grace note.

finger.description: Picking-hand finger: T thumb, I index, M middle, R ring, P pinky.

lh.description: Left-hand finger: 0 open, 1 index, 2 middle, 3 ring, 4 pinky.

dyn.description: Dynamic level of this note (added in 1.2): fff ff f mf mp p pp, loudest first. Appears only when it differs from its track's level (a track with no dyn is at f). A tied note carries none.
